question: What is the best way to give pain medication to a dying patient in constant pain?

options.A: Around the clock on a regular schedule to prevent pain
options.B: When the family expresses concern about visible discomfort
options.C: Every time the blood pressure drops below normal limits
options.D: Only when the patient specifically asks for relief

explanation: Staying ahead of the pain with a regular schedule keeps the patient comfortable, rather than waiting for them to hurt before reacting. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why do endocrine disorders often cause symptoms all over the body in different organs?

options.A: Endocrine glands are physically connected to every single organ in the human body
options.B: Hormones travel systemically through the bloodstream to reach many different target tissues
options.C: The liver automatically spreads hormone imbalances to the digestive tract
options.D: Hormone receptors are identical across all types of tissues and organs

explanation: Hormones are chemical messengers that travel far and wide through the bloodstream. If there's too much or too little of one, every organ that has receptors for it will feel the impact! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T13#GNS222_U2_T13_h8)

question: What should a nurse do when family members demand full resuscitation, but the patient has a valid, documented DNR (Do Not Resuscitate) order?

options.A: Call the police immediately to remove the family
options.B: Hide the medical chart so the family cannot see it
options.C: Ignore the DNR and follow the family's verbal demands
options.D: Uphold the patient's documented wishes while providing compassionate support to the family

explanation: The patient's legally documented wishes always come first. At the same time, we support the grieving family with empathy and clear communication. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h5)

question: What is a major worry when pancreatic fluid leaks from the surgical site after a Whipple procedure?

options.A: Pancreatic fistula and infection
options.B: Immediate high blood pressure
options.C: Chronic kidney stone formation
options.D: Sudden permanent liver failure

explanation: Good to know! A leak at the surgical join creates a pancreatic fistula, which can spill harsh digestive juices into the belly and cause a severe infection. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h8)

question: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, a serious memory problem linked to heavy drinking, is caused by a shortage of which nutrient?

options.A: Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C)
options.B: Thiamine (Vitamin B1)
options.C: Calcium and magnesium
options.D: Iron and folic acid

explanation: Heavy drinking messes with how the body absorbs nutrients. Lacking Vitamin B1 (thiamine) can lead to severe, lasting brain issues if not caught and treated early. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T013#GNS227_U4_T013_h4)

question: What does 'trauma-informed care' mean when nursing a survivor of forced marriage?

options.A: Forcing the patient to recount every traumatic event immediately
options.B: Relying solely on medication to solve the patient's emotional pain
options.C: Allowing family members to make all medical decisions for the patient
options.D: Prioritizing the patient's safety, trust, and control in every interaction

explanation: Trauma-informed care centers on rebuilding the patient's sense of safety, empowerment, and trust in healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is the go-to, first-line drug recommended to prevent postpartum haemorrhage right after delivery?

options.A: Nifedipine
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Hydralazine
options.D: Magnesium sulfate

explanation: Oxytocin is our superstar drug here! It safely helps the uterus contract down firmly to keep heavy bleeding away. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h4)

question: What usually happens when the delicate hormonal balance of the female reproductive system is disrupted?

options.A: Secondary sex characteristics reverse themselves instantly
options.B: Estrogen production permanently stops across all age groups
options.C: The reproductive organs immediately undergo complete atrophy
options.D: It can lead to issues ranging from irregular periods to more serious health concerns

explanation: Think of hormones like a delicate chain reaction! When one part is out of balance, it can throw off the whole cycle, leading to skipped periods or other reproductive challenges. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h1)

question: How do we describe disease spread caused by a mosquito bite?

options.A: Vector-borne transmission
options.B: Direct transmission
options.C: Airborne transmission
options.D: Vehicle-borne transmission

explanation: Easy peasy! Insects like mosquitoes act as 'vectors'—little transport vehicles carrying germs from one person or animal to another. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T87#GNS214_U1_T87_h3)

question: A patient with long-term, poorly controlled diabetes complains of a burning, electric-shock feeling in their feet. What kind of pain is this?

options.A: Acute somatic pain
options.B: Visceral nociceptive pain
options.C: Referred inflammatory pain
options.D: Neuropathic pain

explanation: Spot on! When nerves themselves get damaged (like from high blood sugar over time), they misfire, causing those classic burning, shooting, or electric sensations. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T7#GNS221_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is a main reason fresh fruits spoil so fast after harvest in hot climates?

options.A: Excessive consumption of vegetables by local farmers
options.B: Inadequate cold storage and refrigeration facilities
options.C: Overly strict international export quality standards
options.D: The use of organic seeds instead of commercial hybrids

explanation: Correct! Without good refrigeration in hot weather, fresh produce unfortunately goes bad before it ever gets to market. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T030#GNS227_U2_T030_h7)

question: When should you definitely reach for good old soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.B: Immediately after removing clean non-sterile gloves
options.C: Before touching a client who has a respiratory illness
options.D: When entering a home where clean water is expensive

explanation: You got it! Hand sanitisers are great, but if your hands have physical dirt or fluids on them, you need a proper wash with soap and water. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T9#GNS324_U6_T9_h3)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to assess a patient's spiritual needs even if they do not share the same religious beliefs?

options.A: Because spiritual distress can cause deep emotional and physical suffering
options.B: To satisfy mandatory legal requirements for hospital discharge
options.C: Because chaplains are not allowed to speak with patients alone
options.D: To convert the patient to the nurse's personal faith

explanation: Spiritual health directly impacts overall well-being and comfort, making assessment crucial for comprehensive palliative nursing care regardless of personal beliefs. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h4)

question: What is your very first nursing action if an abdominal wound suddenly pops open and organs are exposed?

options.A: Cover the organs with sterile saline-soaked dressings and call the surgeon.
options.B: Use your gloved fingers to push the organs back inside.
options.C: Wrap a tight binder around the belly to squeeze the organs back in.
options.D: Leave the wound completely open to the fresh air.

explanation: Keep those exposed organs moist with sterile saline gauze so they don't dry out while you call for emergency surgical help. Emergency handled like a champ! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h8)

question: Why must clinic staff record refrigerator temperatures at least twice every single day?

options.A: To calculate the exact electricity bill for the vaccine unit
options.B: To catch and correct temperature excursions before vaccines spoil
options.C: To make sure the electric fan spins at maximum speed
options.D: To fulfill government paperwork requirements with no real benefit

explanation: Routine checks allow nurses to spot equipment failures early and move vaccines to safety before they are ruined. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h4)

question: Which group of people has a naturally higher risk for bone density loss and fractures?

options.A: Professional athletes
options.B: Active teenagers
options.C: Young children
options.D: Older adults

explanation: Aging naturally leads to a gradual reduction in bone density and muscle mass, increasing fracture risks. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h2)

question: What is a major benefit of involving community health workers in post-abortion care programs?

options.A: They manufacture affordable modern contraceptives locally
options.B: They replace doctors and nurses in urban teaching hospitals
options.C: They help educate the public and guide women to facilities early
options.D: They perform surgical manual vacuum aspirations in rural homes

explanation: You got it! Community workers are vital links who spot danger signs early and direct women to get proper medical help. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h6)

question: A young girl who survived breast ironing displays intense social withdrawal and low self-esteem. What is the primary cause of these emotional issues?

options.A: Her inability to understand simple classroom instructions
options.B: Side effects from emergency medications given at the hospital
options.C: Distortion of her natural body image during puberty
options.D: A sudden chemical imbalance in her brain caused by fever

explanation: Unnatural changes and scarring to the chest during developmental years heavily damage self-perception and confidence. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h5)

question: What physical sign helps a nurse tell a breast abscess apart from simple mastitis?

options.A: Mild tenderness without skin changes
options.B: Absence of any systemic fever
options.C: A distinct, fluctuating, fluid-filled mass
options.D: General warmth across the entire chest

explanation: An abscess forms a walled-off pocket of pus that feels spongy or bouncy (fluctuating) under the fingers. Spot on! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T025#GNS226_U3_T025_h6)

question: Who holds primary professional accountability when a nurse administers treatment using a standing order?

options.A: The patient who agreed to visit the primary health care clinic
options.B: The nurse who performed the assessment and administered the treatment
options.C: The federal ministry of health official who printed the guideline booklet
options.D: The pharmaceutical company that manufactured the prescribed drug

explanation: Even when following a standing order, the individual clinician remains legally and professionally responsible for their direct actions and assessments. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h2)

question: How should therapeutic activities in adult day care be viewed?

options.A: As optional events that have no real health benefits
options.B: As purposeful interventions to enhance physical and cognitive well-being
options.C: As mandatory physical punishment for uncooperative behavior
options.D: As simple distractions to keep clients quiet until closing time

explanation: Activities are carefully chosen therapeutic tools designed to maintain mobility, stimulate memory, and promote social connection. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h5)

question: You walk into the main operating room where a patient's abdomen is open. What must you wear in this restricted zone?

options.A: An isolation gown and sterile gloves only
options.B: Surgical scrubs, head cover, and a surgical mask
options.C: Clean street clothes with a disposable plastic apron
options.D: A lab coat worn over casual clothes

explanation: When heading into the restricted zone, full theatre gear (scrubs, cap, and mask) is a must to keep stray hairs and respiratory droplets away from the sterile field. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h2)

question: How do lipid-soluble (steroid) hormones usually work inside a cell?

options.A: By using second messengers on the outside of the cell membrane
options.B: By blocking enzyme actions directly in the extracellular fluid
options.C: By binding to internal receptors and altering gene expression
options.D: By destroying the cell membrane to release stored energy

explanation: Because they love fats, steroid hormones slide right through the cell membrane, head inside, and talk directly to the cell's DNA to make new proteins. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T5#GNS211_U1_T5_h2)

question: A patient on a continuous insulin drip in the ward needs which type of monitoring?

options.A: Testing only when they feel thirsty
options.B: A fasting test once a week
options.C: Capillary checks once a month at home
options.D: Frequent scheduled blood glucose checks

explanation: Insulin drips lower blood sugar fast! Regular checks keep the patient safe from sudden crashes. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why is community education just as important as legal bans when fighting to eliminate FGM?

options.A: Healthcare workers are not allowed to read legal documents
options.B: Community education changes cultural beliefs and tackles the root causes
options.C: Community leaders demand payment to obey the law
options.D: Laws are too expensive to print and distribute

explanation: You got it! While laws set the rules, stopping deep-seated traditions requires educating community members so they choose to leave the practice behind. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h8)

question: Which common substance must a patient recovering from viral hepatitis strictly avoid?

options.A: Alcohol
options.B: Plain water
options.C: Green vegetables
options.D: Fresh fruits

explanation: You got it! Alcohol is processed directly by the liver, so drinking it adds heavy toxic stress to an organ that is already struggling to heal. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h6)

question: What is the main difference between recruitment and selection?

options.A: Recruitment fires poor workers, while selection hires new replacements
options.B: Recruitment tests practical skills, while selection writes the job description
options.C: Recruitment is done only internally, while selection is done only externally
options.D: Recruitment attracts applicants, while selection chooses the best candidate

explanation: Easy way to remember: recruitment casts a wide net to get people to apply, while selection is the screening process where you pick the best person for the job. [learn more](GST321_U4_T1#GST321_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary difference between hearing and active listening?

options.A: Active listening only happens during telephone conversations
options.B: Hearing requires the nurse to take detailed written notes
options.C: Active listening requires full concentration and understanding
options.D: Hearing is a deliberate skill that takes years to learn

explanation: Hearing is just the physical detection of sound, whereas active listening is a conscious mental effort to comprehend the speaker's message and feelings. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h4)

question: What happens during the progressive stage of shock?

options.A: Organs begin to regenerate damaged cells rapidly
options.B: Compensatory mechanisms fail and blood pressure drops
options.C: The body completely recovers its normal metabolic rate
options.D: Blood pressure rises above normal due to fluid retention

explanation: When compensation fails, blood pressure falls and perfusion to vital organs becomes dangerously low. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which piece of equipment is primarily used to elicit deep tendon reflexes during a neurological exam?

options.A: Reflex hammer
options.B: Penlight
options.C: Ophthalmoscope
options.D: Tongue depressor

explanation: A reflex hammer is the standard tool used to gently tap tendons and assess spinal reflex arcs. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h3)

question: If an older adult is denied necessary food, medication, and basic hygiene, what type of abuse is this?

options.A: Psychological abuse
options.B: Physical abuse
options.C: Neglect
options.D: Financial exploitation

explanation: Neglect is when a caregiver fails to provide the basic physical and medical care needed for health and safety. Good job keeping this in mind! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T10#GNS324_U3_T10_h2)

question: When should a safety sharps container be sealed and replaced?

options.A: Whenever a new nursing shift begins

options.C: At the end of every working week regardless of level
options.D: When it reaches the three-quarters full mark

question: What makes an expected outcome (goal) well-written?

options.A: It must be measurable and time-bound
options.B: It should describe what the nurse will do
options.C: It should be as broad as possible
options.D: It must focus on hospital routines

explanation: Goals need clear targets and deadlines (like 'patient will walk to the door by tomorrow') so you can easily tell if they were actually reached. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T7#GNS123_U4_T7_h4)

question: How is chronic urinary retention different from acute urinary retention?

options.A: It involves painful spasms of the ureters.
options.B: It causes complete kidney shutdown right away.
options.C: It develops slowly and is often painless.
options.D: It only happens to younger female patients.

explanation: Because chronic retention builds up gradually, the bladder stretches out slowly over time, so the patient usually doesn't feel severe, sudden pain. Great job thinking it through! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT part of a nurse's core responsibility when giving medications?

options.A: Checking the patient for known drug allergies beforehand
options.B: Deciding the wholesale market price for the medication
options.C: Verifying the correct dosage calculation prior to giving it
options.D: Teaching the patient about possible side effects at home

explanation: Pricing medications is up to the pharmacy and hospital administration—your focus is purely on safe, clinical care and patient education! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T4#GNS125_U2_T4_h8)

question: What is the main goal of doing a secondary survey in critical care?

options.A: To administer routine scheduled morning drugs
options.B: To uncover hidden injuries or underlying problems
options.C: To discharge the patient from the hospital ward
options.D: To replace the need for laboratory blood tests

explanation: The head-to-toe secondary exam helps you find any sneaky injuries or issues that might have hidden during the fast primary survey. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h3)

question: What major postpartum emergency is an anaemic woman most at risk for?

options.A: Sudden closing of her airway
options.B: Sudden buildup of amniotic fluid
options.C: Hypovolemic shock from normal blood loss
options.D: Temporary leg paralysis

question: In the pain assessment mnemonic OPQRSTUV, what does the letter 'Q' stand for?

options.A: Quantity
options.B: Quickness
options.C: Quietness
options.D: Quality

explanation: The letter Q refers to quality, prompting the nurse to ask what the pain actually feels like to the patient. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T5#GNS321_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which hormone keeps the uterus relaxed throughout pregnancy to prevent early labor?

options.A: progesterone
options.B: estrogen
options.C: oxytocin
options.D: prolactin

explanation: You got it! Progesterone is the main pregnancy-maintaining hormone that keeps the uterine muscles calm until it is time for delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h2)

question: What is the main job of an analgesic drug?

options.A: To relieve pain without causing unconsciousness
options.B: To reduce high body temperature quickly
options.C: To put the patient into a deep sleep
options.D: To lower elevated blood pressure readings

explanation: Analgesics are medicines that chase away pain while keeping your patient awake and alert so you can still talk to them! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T2#GNS223_U5_T2_h1)

question: How far do infectious respiratory droplets typically travel through the air?

options.A: Throughout the ventilation system
options.B: Up to ten meters
options.C: Across an entire building
options.D: Less than one meter

question: What is a flat, discolored skin lesion that is less than 1 cm wide called?

options.A: Papule
options.B: Nodule
options.C: Plaque
options.D: Macule

question: What is the primary role of red bone marrow found inside bones?

options.A: Storing excess body fat
options.B: Producing new blood cells
options.C: Releasing calcium into joints
options.D: Filtering waste from blood

explanation: Red bone marrow contains stem cells responsible for creating red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T1#GNS222_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which blood test is the most reliable sign that heart muscle cells have been damaged?

options.A: Troponin
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Blood urea nitrogen
options.D: Serum electrolytes

question: Which group of people suffers the most from poor environmental hygiene?

options.A: Teenagers in secondary schools
options.B: Children under five years old
options.C: Middle-aged office workers
options.D: Healthy young adult athletes

explanation: You're right! Little ones are still developing their immunity, making them extra vulnerable to severe dehydration from tummy bugs. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h6)

question: What is an important feature of the data you get from using the sisterhood method?

question: A patient is having a rising panic attack at home. What is the best immediate nursing action?

options.C: Leave the patient completely alone in a dark room until they calm down

question: A patient is scheduled for a surgical procedure on both legs requiring complete lower body numbness without general anesthesia. Which route of administration is the surgical team most likely to select?

options.A: Subcutaneous
options.B: Intrathecal
options.C: Intramuscular
options.D: Transdermal

question: Where are ganglia located in the human body?

options.A: Within the center of the spinal cord
options.B: Outside the central nervous system
options.C: Directly on skeletal muscle fibers
options.D: Inside the cerebral cortex only

explanation: You can picture ganglia as little relay stations located out in the peripheral nervous system, away from the brain and spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T16#GNS211_U3_T16_h2)

question: A male patient insists he doesn't have an STI because his sores don't hurt. How should you gently correct him?

options.B: Some serious infections like syphilis can cause painless sores in their early stages

options.D: Painless sores always indicate a non-infectious skin allergy rather than an STI

question: In the RICE first-aid treatment for sprains, what does the letter 'I' stand for?

options.A: Immobilization
options.B: Ice
options.C: Injection
options.D: Inflammation

explanation: Ice is applied early on to narrow blood vessels (vasoconstriction), which keeps swelling down and helps numb the pain. Great nursing intervention to know! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T9#GNS222_U1_T9_h4)

question: In the Health Belief Model, what do we mean by 'perceived susceptibility'?

options.A: A reminder from a family member to visit the clinic

options.C: The financial cost of buying hospital drugs
options.D: Thinking a disease has no cure at all

question: Why is blunt heart injury often harder to spot right away compared to a stab wound?

options.A: X-ray machines cannot take pictures of blunt force trauma.
options.B: The chest wall often shows no open wounds or obvious external damage.
options.C: The heart stops beating completely right away.
options.D: Symptoms only appear several weeks after the accident.

question: Why does a person trapped in a smoke-filled room suffer from asphyxia?

options.A: Severe dehydration and low blood volume
options.B: Toxic gas inhalation replacing ambient oxygen
options.C: Allergic reaction to dust particles
options.D: Sudden paralysis of the heart muscle

question: What does the letter 'A' stand for in the SBAR communication framework?

options.A: Assessment
options.B: Antibiotic
options.C: Admission
options.D: Aftercare

question: Why should nurses always focus on 'felt needs' (real problems the community faces daily) when planning education?

options.A: It guarantees immediate financial funding from donors
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to prepare visual aids
options.C: Learners pay closer attention to problems they actually experience

explanation: People naturally care more about health issues affecting their everyday lives than abstract or distant theories. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h3)

question: Why must a delivery kit with a torn or punctured wrapper be discarded or replaced?

options.A: The items inside will be too cold
options.B: The plastic becomes toxic over time
options.C: The manufacturer voids the warranty
options.D: The sterile barrier is broken

question: What is the main reason we use X-rays and scans in bone and muscle nursing?

options.A: To visualize bone, joints, and soft tissues for diagnosis and monitoring
options.B: To administer direct chemical treatment into the bone marrow
options.C: To replace physical assessment and hands-on patient evaluation
options.D: To permanently destroy damaged musculoskeletal cells and tissues

question: Besides keeping the skin clean, what is a key benefit of bathing a bedridden patient?

options.A: Preventing the patient from ever developing a fever
options.B: Completely eliminating the need for any pain medication
options.C: Stimulating blood circulation and assessing skin integrity
options.D: Lowering the patient's blood pressure permanently

question: Why do we encourage new mothers to get up and walk around (ambulate) early after childbirth?

options.B: To reduce the risk of blood clots and improve circulation
options.C: To encourage the baby to sleep through the night
options.D: To prevent the mother from producing too much colostrum

question: Which of these is NOT a typical long-term complication of untreated polycythaemia vera?

question: How are mobile phones and digital tools currently used in public health nursing?

question: What do we call the medical condition where the upper back curves outward into a hunchback shape?

question: What hormone drives the growth of an ER-positive breast cancer tumor?

question: A patient with a history of heavy drinking stumbles when walking and has jerky eye movements. What should you suspect?

question: A child who quickly masters tough math concepts and deep thinking is showing signs of what?

question: What is the preferred way to feed a patient with a major burn injury?

question: What happens when antibodies in a patient's plasma encounter unfamiliar red blood cell antigens?

question: What is the best nursing action when taking care of a patient with a bleeding disorder?

question: Why do nurses need to understand how different imaging tests work?

question: What is a likely result of poor family planning counselling?

question: What is a major physiological function of the hypodermis?

question: Why is it so important for nurses to check in on a patient's mental health during post-abortion care?

question: What is the most important infection control practice for a family caregiver managing a home gastrostomy tube?

question: What is the most important thing a nurse should do when abnormal moulding shows up on the partograph?

question: What is a key job of interneurons in a reflex pathway?

question: If a patient's skin suddenly turns pale and blotchy during cold therapy, what should you do?

question: What is an important nursing task for the AED right after a emergency code is over?

question: Which of these is an environmental hazard that can cause falls at home?

question: What is the main purpose of using the teach-back method during patient education?

question: Which body systems work together to create coordinated movement?

question: What is the immediate first-aid action a nurse should take after sustaining a needle-stick injury?

question: Why is newborn screening so important for babies with sickle cell anaemia?

question: How do blood-borne pathogens usually spread during unsafe injection practices?

question: Why are electrolytes important for the body?

question: Which part of the ear contains the special structures that handle both your hearing and your sense of balance?

question: Why is advocating for good patient nutrition such a big deal in modern nursing?

question: Why do nurses monitor hourly urine output so closely when caring for a patient in shock?

question: What is Chadwick's sign?

question: What does a low Height-for-Age measurement tell you about a child?

question: What is the main goal of post-abortion care (PAC) counselling?

question: Why should you always talk to an unconscious patient before doing a procedure?

question: What is the best way to support parents who are grieving a baby's birth defect?

question: Why should you let the alcohol swab dry completely on the skin before giving an injection?

question: How might a depressed older adult unusually show their emotional pain?

question: When should you perform abdominal thrusts on a choking victim?

question: Which leadership style works best with the core philosophy of team nursing?

question: Which scenario represents a violation of the 'right time' medication principle?

question: Which piece of equipment do you need to safely connect an oxygen mask to a hospital wall supply?

question: Which primary brain swelling (vesicle) grows into the cerebrum?

question: You suspect a patient is skipping their blood pressure meds because their readings are still high. How should you start this chat?

question: A patient asks how eating more vegetables and whole grains helps their heart. What is the best nursing explanation?

options.A: They replace the need to ever check your blood pressure again

question: When a patient suddenly stands up and feels dizzy from a drop in blood pressure, how does the body normally respond?

options.C: Shuts down vasomotor tone to pool blood in the lower limbs

question: Why is insulin considered the preferred medication for managing diabetes during pregnancy?

question: Why must a patient taking the blood thinner warfarin watch how many leafy green vegetables they eat?

question: What is the single best way to stop infectious diarrhoea from spreading in a community?

question: Why is a Venturi mask often chosen for patients with COPD?

question: What is the main laboratory test used to detect chlamydia and gonorrhea from a swab or urine sample?

question: What does it usually mean if a patient's urea level is very high compared to their creatinine?

question: A clinic kitchen has a very strict food budget for the month. What is the best way to handle food purchasing?

question: Why is active community surveillance just as important as checking hospital record books?

question: Why are birth control pills often given to a patient with functional ovarian cysts?

question: Why do nursing leaders study diffusion theories when introducing a new practice?

question: What does the accessibility principle mean in youth-friendly health services?

question: Why are older adults much more likely to become dehydrated?

options.A: Water is absorbed too quickly by their stomach
options.B: They have a decreased sense of thirst
options.C: They sweat much more than younger people
options.D: Their kidneys stop producing urine entirely

explanation: Spot on! The natural aging process slows down the body's thirst signals, so older adults often don't feel thirsty even when their bodies are crying out for water. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T4#GNS321_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which ethical principle is all about actively doing good and helping your patient?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Autonomy
options.C: Veracity
options.D: Justice

explanation: Think of Beneficence as your active duty to do good and boost the health and well-being of everyone in your care. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why is the sequence of techniques changed when examining the abdomen?

options.A: Auscultation is done first so pressing on the belly does not change bowel sounds
options.B: Percussion is omitted entirely to prevent patient discomfort
options.C: Inspection is skipped because visual data is unreliable
options.D: Palpation must be done first to locate hidden organs before listening

explanation: Touching or pressing the abdomen can stimulate bowel activity, giving a false impression of bowel sounds. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h6)

question: Which factor can cause a pulse oximeter sensor to give an inaccurate reading on a patient's finger?

options.A: Cold fingers and poor peripheral circulation
options.B: Speaking in a normal tone of voice during the test
options.C: Drinking a glass of cold water before testing
options.D: A high room temperature on the hospital ward

explanation: Pulse oximeters rely on good blood flow through the finger; if circulation is sluggish or cold, the machine cannot read the pulse well. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is a simple, free way that nurse leaders can boost daily morale on the ward?

options.A: Threatening disciplinary action for minor errors
options.B: Recognizing and acknowledging a job well done
options.C: Ignoring daily shift complaints to save time
options.D: Mandating extra weekend shifts without overtime

explanation: A simple 'Thank you, you handled that emergency brilliantly!' goes a very long way in making a nurse feel valued. [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is a major risk for a surgical patient whose stress is left unmanaged after an operation?

options.A: Decreased need for pain medication because adrenaline numbs nerves
options.B: Rapid healing caused by continuous high cortisol output
options.C: Lowered blood pressure preventing any risk of postoperative bleeding
options.D: Increased risk of infection due to suppressed immune function

explanation: When stress hormones stay high, they weaken the immune system, making it much easier for post-op patients to pick up infections. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h8)

question: What type of tissue makes up uterine fibroids?

options.A: Malignant epithelial tissue
options.B: Infected lymphatic fluid
options.C: Hardened calcified bone
options.D: Benign smooth muscle cells

explanation: Correct! Fibroids (also called leiomyomas) are simply non-cancerous growths made of the uterus's own smooth muscle cells. Nothing to panic about! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T19#GNS216_U5_T19_h2)

question: Who are some of the best local partners for community health nurses working to prevent FGM?

options.A: Religious leaders, school teachers, and women's groups
options.B: International lawyers and foreign embassy officials only
options.C: Private security guards and military personnel exclusively
options.D: Traditional cutters and commercial blade suppliers

explanation: Correct! Teaming up with respected community voices helps nurses reach families effectively and spread the message against FGM. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T5#GNS225_U6_T5_h7)

question: Why is it usually recommended to take oral corticosteroid pills with meals or food?

options.A: To speed up the absorption of the drug through the intestinal wall
options.B: To completely eliminate the risk of developing systemic fluid retention
options.C: To minimize stomach irritation and reduce the risk of gastrointestinal ulcers
options.D: To prevent the medication from altering the patient's morning blood glucose

explanation: Steroids can be tough on the stomach lining and increase acid. Taking them with food acts like a cozy blanket to protect the stomach from irritation and ulcers. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h8)

question: Which of these is a mineral-based drug commonly used to neutralize stomach acid?

options.A: Penicillin G
options.B: Morphine sulfate
options.C: Digoxin extract
options.D: Calcium carbonate

explanation: Calcium carbonate is a mineral compound often found in over-the-counter antacids to quickly soothe heartburn. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T5#GNS125_U2_T5_h4)

question: Where are the intercostal nerves located?

options.A: Deep in the neck muscles
options.B: In the lower back near the pelvis
options.C: In the spaces between the ribs
options.D: Along the front of the thighs

explanation: Intercostal nerves travel directly within the intercostal spaces between the ribs to supply the chest wall and intercostal muscles. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h6)

question: What is the main job of a medical-surgical nurse?

options.A: Managing administrative budgets for hospital wards and clinics
options.B: Caring for adult patients with various medical illnesses and surgical needs
options.C: Delivering emergency psychiatric interventions in crisis centers
options.D: Providing specialized surgical operations inside the operating theater

explanation: You'll see med-surg nursing everywhere in the hospital! It's all about looking after adults dealing with medical conditions or bouncing back from surgery. You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U1_T1#GNS123_U1_T1_h1)

question: What does the term 'hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy' mean?

options.A: Sudden inflammation of the peripheral nerve endings
options.B: An infection of the lining surrounding the spinal cord
options.C: Brain injury caused by oxygen and blood deprivation
options.D: A chronic degenerative disease of the liver tissue

explanation: Let's break down the big words: 'hypoxic' (low oxygen), 'ischemic' (low blood flow), and 'encephalopathy' (brain trouble). Put it together, and it's brain injury from lack of oxygen and blood! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T1#GNS112_U7_T1_h7)

question: A patient starts a new antidepressant and soon reports she cannot achieve orgasm, even though she still has normal desire. Which category fits this best?

options.A: Substance/Medication-Induced Sexual Dysfunction
options.B: Genito-Pelvic Pain/Penetration Disorder
options.C: Female Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder
options.D: Primary lifelong orgasmic dysfunction

explanation: Well done! Because the symptom popped up right after starting a specific medication, we link it directly to that substance. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T25#GNS312_U1_T25_h3)

question: Which head measurement presents when the baby's head is tilted all the way back in a brow presentation, making delivery very difficult?

options.A: Suboccipitobregmatic diameter
options.B: Occipitofrontal diameter
options.C: Biparietal diameter
options.D: Mentovertical diameter

explanation: Spot on! At 13.5 cm, the mentovertical diameter is the widest one, and it's usually too big to easily pass through an average pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T10#GNS121_U6_T10_h6)

question: During a home visit, you notice the weights for a patient's skin traction are resting on the floor. What is your very first action?

options.A: Document that the patient is non-compliant with bedrest orders
options.B: Remove the traction setup entirely because it is no longer effective
options.C: Ensure the weights hang freely without touching the floor or bed
options.D: Add extra weight to make up for the time the weights spent resting

explanation: Traction weights must always hang free! If they touch the floor, the pulling force stops, and the bones won't stay aligned. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h5)

question: A pregnant patient comes to the clinic vomiting ten times a day, unable to keep water down, and showing ketones in her urine. What condition is she most likely experiencing?

options.A: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.B: Gestational hypertension
options.C: Normal morning sickness
options.D: Eclamptic seizure

explanation: Uncontrolled vomiting with dehydration, inability to retain fluids, and urinary ketones goes far beyond normal morning sickness into hyperemesis gravidarum. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h2)

question: A patient presents with low blood pressure and dry mucous membranes due to fluid loss. Which nursing intervention best supports fluid homeostasis?

options.A: Administering a medication to raise heart rate
options.B: Encouraging strict bed rest without fluids
options.C: Applying a cooling blanket to lower fever
options.D: Administering prescribed intravenous fluids

explanation: Correct! Giving IV fluids directly replaces the lost volume, bringing blood pressure and circulation back to a safe zone. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T7#GNS123_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which of these terms describes multicellular parasitic worms?

options.A: Bacteria
options.B: Helminths
options.C: Ectoparasites
options.D: Protozoa

explanation: Spot on! Helminths are multicellular worms (like tapeworms and roundworms). Protozoa are tiny and single-celled, while ectoparasites hang out on the outside of the skin. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h1)

question: What is the most important assessment when checking a limb's circulation and nerve function after a joint procedure?

options.A: Measuring the exact circumference of the thigh
options.B: Listening for bowel sounds in the lower abdomen
options.C: Checking the patient's oral temperature reading
options.D: Checking pulse, color, movement, and sensation

explanation: Neurovascular checks (the famous '5 Ps' or pulse, color, movement, and sensation) help you catch any blood flow or nerve issues early before they turn into major complications. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T4#GNS222_U1_T4_h8)

question: A patient with a history of Type I FGM reports pain during sexual intercourse. What is the clinical term for this symptom?

options.A: Amenorrhea
options.B: Menorrhagia
options.C: Dysmenorrhea
options.D: Dyspareunia

explanation: Painful intercourse is called dyspareunia. It's a very common long-term challenge caused by scarring in the genital tissue. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T3#GNS312_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which bacteria is most commonly linked to undercooked poultry and eggs?

options.A: Vibrio
options.B: Shigella
options.C: Salmonella
options.D: Listeria

explanation: Salmonella loves to hang out in the digestive tracts of chickens and birds, which is why raw eggs and poultry need proper cooking! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h2)

question: Why are vital sign trends over several hours more useful than a single reading?

options.A: They prevent the need to perform laboratory blood tests
options.B: They take less time for the nurse to chart
options.C: They show whether the patient is improving or getting worse over time
options.D: They guarantee that the electronic monitor is working correctly

explanation: Brilliant nursing insight! Tracking patterns helps you catch subtle warning signs before a patient takes a turn for the worse. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T7#GNS123_U1_T7_h5)

question: What strategy is often successful when working with religious leaders to stop harmful traditional customs?

options.A: Replacing traditional ceremonies with foreign cultural festivals
options.B: Reviewing texts to show the practices are cultural, not religious
options.C: Threatening them with immediate excommunication from society
options.D: Banning all places of worship that question government policies

explanation: Many harmful practices are falsely claimed as religious mandates; examining texts helps separate faith from harmful custom. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h4)

question: What extra job does propylthiouracil (PTU) do that methimazole doesn't?

options.A: Stimulating the pituitary gland to stop releasing TSH
options.B: Binding directly to circulating T3 molecules in the blood
options.C: Destroying existing thyroid tissue through direct radiation
options.D: Inhibiting the peripheral conversion of T4 into T3

explanation: Besides stopping new hormone production, PTU also slows down how T4 turns into the active T3 hormone in the body's tissues. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T3#GNS223_U7_T3_h2)

question: During a clinic visit, what sign might make a nurse suspect a young patient is in an early marriage?

options.A: Refusing to answer any questions about her medical history
options.B: Demanding to see the head doctor without family present
options.C: Expressing high levels of satisfaction with her home life
options.D: Hesitation to speak when an older partner answers for her

explanation: A young minor in a forced early union often acts very quiet or lets her older spouse control the entire conversation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T9#GNS312_U1_T9_h6)

question: What usually causes antimicrobial resistance to spread in clinical practice?

options.A: Using combination drug therapy for mycobacterial infections
options.B: Regular handwashing and proper cleaning of hospital equipment
options.C: Administering culture-guided targeted therapy to patients
options.D: Inappropriate use and incomplete courses of anti-infective drugs

explanation: Misusing antibiotics—like taking them for viral colds or stopping halfway—teaches bacteria how to survive our best drugs. Good hand hygiene and smart prescribing protect everyone! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T4#GNS223_U2_T4_h4)

question: A patient comes to the clinic complaining of constant thirst, frequent urination, and sudden weight loss. What condition should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Chronic kidney disease
options.B: Diabetes mellitus
options.C: Urinary tract infection
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: The classic trio of excessive thirst, frequent urination, and unexplained weight loss strongly points toward new-onset diabetes mellitus. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h2)

question: What does the golden nursing rule 'if it wasn't documented, it wasn't done' mean in a court of law?

options.A: Unwritten care cannot be proven to have been given in a court of law
options.B: Verbal reports to doctors hold more legal weight than written notes
options.C: Documentation is more important than actually speaking to the client
options.D: Nurses do not need to perform procedures if they write about them

explanation: Legally, courts rely on written records. If an action is missing from the client's file, it is legally considered not to have happened! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h7)

question: Which past medical history is most important when assessing a male patient's fertility risks?

options.A: A normal resting heart rate and blood pressure reading
options.B: A history of undescended testicles in childhood
options.C: A personal preference for wearing loose cotton clothing
options.D: Occasional mild muscle soreness after heavy exercise

explanation: Undescended testicles mean the tissue spent time exposed to higher core body heat, which can impact future fertility. Great clinical insight to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h8)

question: What is the key difference between active and passive range of motion?

options.A: Active is done by the patient alone, while passive is done with the nurse moving the joint
options.B: Active measures upper body joints, while passive measures lower body joints
options.C: Active is performed while standing, while passive is performed while lying down
options.D: Active uses a goniometer, while passive uses a measuring tape

explanation: Active movement relies on the patient's own muscle power, whereas passive movement relies on the nurse moving the relaxed limb. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which common condition involves the weakening of bone due to rapid mineral loss from the spongy trabeculae?

options.A: Osteoporosis
options.B: Osteomyelitis
options.C: Osteoarthritis
options.D: Osteosarcoma

explanation: You've got this! Osteoporosis means 'porous bones.' It happens when bones lose minerals too quickly, making the tiny spongy struts thin out and break easily. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T3#GNS121_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the purpose of the safety limits (guardrails) on smart infusion pumps?

options.A: To automatically calculate patient drug dosages without nurse input
options.B: To track how many supplies are used during each shift
options.C: To lock the pump door so patients cannot change settings
options.D: To warn nurses if a programmed dose is outside safe limits

explanation: Exactly! Guardrails act like a helpful safety net, popping up a warning if a number looks too high or too low. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T3#GNS212_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why do doctors order a serum creatinine test for a patient with long-term urine retention?

options.A: To determine if the patient has a urinary tract infection
options.B: To evaluate how well the liver is producing proteins
options.C: To check if urine backup is damaging kidney function
options.D: To measure the level of sugar in the circulating blood

explanation: When urine cannot get out, the pressure travels backward up to the kidneys, which can slow down their filtering work. Checking creatinine helps us catch kidney stress early! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h4)

question: What is the main goal of tertiary prevention for someone living with COPD?

options.A: Slowing down the disease and preventing troublesome complications
options.B: Preventing airway inflammation back when they were a child
options.C: Screening healthy family members for hidden lung issues
options.D: Completely curing the permanent damage in the air sacs

explanation: Tertiary prevention steps in after a chronic illness is already present. The aim is to help the patient manage symptoms, stay active, and avoid severe flare-ups. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h6)

question: During an assessment, a patient answers 'yes' to three out of four CAGE questions. What is your best next step as a nurse?

options.A: Tell the patient that drinking is completely normal and requires no action
options.B: Perform a detailed follow-up assessment regarding alcohol use patterns and dependence risks
options.C: Ignore the screening results since CAGE is only meant for research purposes
options.D: Immediately discharge the patient without discussing lifestyle habits

explanation: A high CAGE score is a red flag for possible alcohol dependence. It's time to gently dig deeper and offer supportive guidance. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T013#GNS227_U4_T013_h6)

question: A patient with heart failure repeatedly misses their diuretic medication. What is this patient most likely to experience?

options.A: Severe fluid overload and breathing difficulties
options.B: Lowered blood pressure to normal limits
options.C: Complete recovery from heart muscle weakness
options.D: Rapid weight loss and extreme dehydration

explanation: Diuretics help the body get rid of excess fluid; missing them allows fluid to back up into the lungs, causing severe shortness of breath. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h3)

question: How often should a bedbound patient usually be turned to prevent bedsores?

options.A: Every thirty minutes
options.B: Every two hours
options.C: Once every shift
options.D: Only when they complain of pain

explanation: Turning a patient at least every two hours takes pressure off bony areas and protects their skin from breaking down. Great routine to master for clinicals! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T8#GNS122_U3_T8_h6)

question: What does the term AEFI stand for in public health nursing?

options.A: Adverse Event Following Immunization
options.B: Acute Epidemic Fever Infection
options.C: Annual Evaluation of Facility Infrastructure
options.D: Assigned Emergency First-aid Intervention

explanation: AEFI is the standard global acronym used to describe medical incidents occurring after a person receives a vaccine. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h5)

question: What size of IV catheter is preferred for fast fluid replacement in a severe trauma patient?

options.A: Midline catheter with dual lumens
options.B: Large-bore catheter like 16 or 18 gauge
options.C: Small-bore catheter like 24 gauge
options.D: Peripherally inserted central catheter

explanation: Think of an IV line like a pipe: a wider pipe (16 or 18 gauge) lets fluids and blood flow in much faster during an emergency. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T4#GNS221_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is typically the earliest symptom experienced by someone developing an occupational lung disease?

options.A: A persistent cough and shortness of breath with exertion
options.B: Sudden paralysis of both lower extremities
options.C: Complete loss of the sense of taste and smell
options.D: Bright yellow coloration of the skin and eyes

explanation: Early lung damage usually manifests as a mild, dry cough and breathlessness that only appears when the person engages in physical work or exercise. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h5)

question: A nurse walks into a ward and finds a junior colleague throwing a used syringe into a regular black polythene bag. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Correct the colleague immediately and ensure the syringe is moved to the sharps box
options.B: Ignore the mistake because cleaners will sort it out later anyway
options.C: Write an official query letter to the hospital medical director
options.D: Remove all waste bins from the ward to teach everyone a lesson

explanation: Nurses have a duty to correct segregation errors instantly to maintain a safe working and clinical environment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h7)

question: Who typically acts as the central coordinator connecting various specialists and the patient in clinical settings?

options.A: The hospital accountant
options.B: The facility security guard
options.C: The pharmaceutical supplier
options.D: The nurse

explanation: Nurses coordinate care pathways, schedule referrals, and bridge communication between patients and the multidisciplinary healthcare team. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h7)

question: What treatment involves placing tiny radioactive sources directly inside or close to a cervical tumor?

options.A: Hysterectomy
options.B: Cryotherapy
options.C: Brachytherapy
options.D: Chemotherapy

explanation: You've got it! 'Brachy' means close—so brachytherapy places radiation right next to or inside the tumor to target bad cells while sparing healthy tissue. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h6)

question: When moving an injured person, what is the most important goal to keep in mind?

options.A: Reaching the nearest hospital in the shortest possible time
options.B: Ensuring the patient's family members can ride along
options.C: Clearing the emergency scene before law enforcement arrives
options.D: Moving the patient safely without causing further injury

explanation: You've got this! Safety and protecting the patient from extra harm always come first, even before rushing to the hospital. Great nursing instincts! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T10#GNS112_U7_T10_h1)

question: A patient has been dealing with severe chronic financial and physical stress for over a year and now has a failing immune system and frequent infections. Which stage of GAS are they experiencing?

options.A: Stage of resistance
options.B: Homeostatic baseline stage
options.C: Stage of exhaustion
options.D: Alarm reaction stage

explanation: Prolonged stress depletes the body's energy reserves, leading to organ failure and immune collapse during the exhaustion stage. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h2)

question: What type of food should make up the biggest part of an adolescent girl's daily energy intake?

options.A: Refined table sugars
options.B: Pure protein powders
options.C: Saturated animal fats
options.D: Complex carbohydrates

explanation: Wonderful! Complex carbs (like yam, brown rice, and beans) give growing teens steady, lasting energy and healthy fiber. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T010#GNS227_U2_T010_h4)

question: What happens to an ATP molecule after it gives energy to a cell?

options.A: It loses a phosphate group and turns into ADP
options.B: It gains an extra nitrogen atom and becomes a lipid
options.C: It splits entirely into four separate water molecules
options.D: It binds permanently to a red blood cell for transport

explanation: When ATP spends its energy, it releases one of its phosphate groups and becomes ADP (adenosine diphosphate). It is like a spent battery waiting to be recharged! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T8#GNS121_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the primary cause of a vasovagal reaction during cervical manipulation or MVA?

options.A: An acute drop in the patient's body temperature
options.B: Complete blockage of the airway by mucus
options.C: Sudden stimulation of nerves around the cervix
options.D: A severe allergic reaction to the plastic syringe

explanation: Stretching or manipulating the cervix triggers nerve responses that can lower the heart rate and blood pressure, causing fainting or dizziness. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h7)

question: A nurse is caring for a patient from a remote mountainous region with high rates of goiter. What public health program should the nurse support?

options.A: Teaching deep-sea fishing techniques
options.B: Introducing desert camel farming
options.C: Building large industrial rice mills
options.D: Promoting universal salt iodization programs

explanation: Mountain areas often lack iodine in their local soil and food, making iodized salt the best and easiest way to protect community health. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T022#GNS227_U2_T022_h8)

question: A community action plan includes assigning specific tasks to local youth groups. What is the main benefit of this?

options.A: It guarantees that international donors will send more money
options.B: It builds local capacity and ensures project sustainability
options.C: It eliminates the need for any monitoring or supervision
options.D: It prevents the nurses from doing any actual field work

explanation: Involving local groups builds their skills and ensures the community can maintain the health interventions long after external nurses leave. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h6)

question: When we talk about 'somatosensation', what kind of feelings are we including?

options.A: Balance and equilibrium
options.B: Taste and smell
options.C: Body position and pain
options.D: Vision and hearing

explanation: Great try! Somatosensation covers all the general body feelings like touch, temperature, pain, and knowing where your limbs are. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T11#GNS211_U4_T11_h1)

question: In the very first hour after delivery (the fourth stage), how often should you check the mother's vital signs and womb tone?

options.A: Every 4 hours
options.B: Every 15 minutes
options.C: Every 5 minutes
options.D: Every hour

explanation: Keep shining! Because the risk of bleeding is highest right after birth, we monitor her closely every 15 minutes during that first hour. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T006#GNS226_U3_T006_h7)

question: When should a patient's nutritional screening take place in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Promptly upon admission to identify risks early.
options.B: Only if the doctor notices visible weight loss.
options.C: Only after the patient requests a special diet from the kitchen.
options.D: Just before the patient is discharged home.

explanation: Early screening on admission helps nurses and clinicians spot nutritional vulnerabilities before they cause severe clinical complications. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h6)

question: During a postnatal home visit, why do you gently feel (palpate) the mother's lower tummy?

options.A: To align the spine of the postpartum mother
options.B: To check if the uterus is contracting firmly and shrinking
options.C: To stimulate milk production in the mammary glands
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the new baby

explanation: A firm uterus means it's clamping down properly, which stops bleeding from where the placenta was attached. That's a huge relief for postpartum recovery! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h5)

question: Which group of patients is excused from fasting in almost all major religions?

options.A: The sick, pregnant women, and the elderly
options.B: Individuals traveling outside their home country
options.C: Only children under the age of five years
options.D: Athletes and people engaged in heavy manual labor

explanation: Major religions always put health and safety first, offering clear exemptions from fasting for vulnerable groups like the sick, pregnant women, and the elderly. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T019#GNS227_U2_T019_h7)

question: What protective item must be given to a patient before entering the MRI scanner to protect their ears?

options.A: A thick cotton neck brace
options.B: Soft foam earplugs or headphones
options.C: A sterile surgical face mask
options.D: A lead-lined protective apron

explanation: Great! MRI machines make a loud knocking sound, so ear protection is a must to keep the patient comfortable. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the main job of the urethral sphincter in normal bladder control?

options.A: To sense when the bladder is completely full
options.B: To push urine out of the bladder during voiding
options.C: To stay contracted and maintain a tight seal against urine leakage
options.D: To stretch when the bladder fills with urine

explanation: The urethral sphincter acts like a tight valve, staying closed to keep urine inside until you're ready to use the bathroom. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h2)

question: A patient has delivered two full-term babies, had one early miscarriage, and has two living children. What is her parity?

options.A: Three
options.B: Four
options.C: Two
options.D: Five

explanation: You've got this! Parity counts pregnancies that made it past 20 weeks (viable births). Since she had two full-term deliveries, her parity is 2. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T3#GNS311_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the right speed for doing chest compressions on an adult?

options.A: 80 to 100 compressions
options.B: 60 to 80 compressions
options.C: 100 to 120 compressions
options.D: 140 to 160 compressions

explanation: Aim for 100 to 120 per minute—think of the beat of the song 'Stayin' Alive'! It pumps blood well without wearing you out too fast. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T7#GNS321_U2_T7_h3)

question: Where are the ureters positioned in the tummy area?

options.A: Subcutaneous position just beneath the skin
options.B: Medial position inside the peritoneal cavity
options.C: Intraperitoneal position floating near the liver
options.D: Retroperitoneal position along the posterior wall

explanation: Great try! They sit outside the main tummy cavity, running quietly down the back wall behind the peritoneum. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T2#GNS121_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which of these phrases is too vague and should be avoided when charting a neurological assessment?

options.A: GCS score is 15
options.B: Hand grip strength is 5 out of 5
options.C: Pupils are 3mm and briskly reactive
options.D: Patient is normal

explanation: 'Normal' means different things to different people. Always write clear, measurable findings like pupil sizes and GCS scores! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T4#GNS222_U3_T4_h8)

question: Why is it important to involve bedside nurses when drafting clinical standards?

options.A: They perform the actual care and understand practical floor realities
options.B: It guarantees that hospital funding will increase
options.C: It removes the need for any supervisory oversight
options.D: They are the only ones allowed to sign administrative policies

explanation: Frontline nurses know what works in daily practice, making their input vital for creating realistic and usable standards. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h4)

question: What is a common physical sign that an adolescent is experiencing chronic emotional stress from unsupportive relationships?

options.A: A permanent change in natural eye color
options.B: Sudden increase in height and shoe size
options.C: Rapid healing of minor skin scratches
options.D: Frequent unexplained headaches and stomachaches

explanation: Emotional distress often shows up as physical symptoms, known as somatic complaints, when teenagers face toxic environments at home or school. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h3)

question: Postmenopausal women are at a higher risk for which bone condition because their hormone levels drop?

options.A: Osteoporosis
options.B: Septic arthritis
options.C: Muscular dystrophy
options.D: Acute osteomyelitis

explanation: You got it! The drop in estrogen after menopause speeds up bone loss, putting older women at high risk for osteoporosis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T2#GNS222_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the immediate drug of choice for managing severe anaphylactic shock following a vaccination?

options.A: Oral paracetamol syrup
options.B: Intravenous normal saline
options.C: Subcutaneous hydrocortisone
options.D: Intramuscular epinephrine

explanation: Epinephrine is the life-saving treatment for anaphylaxis because it quickly constricts blood vessels, relaxes airway passages, and raises dropping blood pressure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h7)

question: What is the main goal of Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) in public health?

options.A: To promote positive and healthy behaviour choices
options.B: To replace modern medicine with traditional remedies
options.C: To distribute free medical equipment to hospitals
options.D: To punish communities that ignore health guidelines

explanation: Spot on! BCC is all about working together with individuals and communities to help them build healthier lifestyle habits. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h1)

question: How do progestin-only implants mainly prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By thickening cervical mucus, stopping ovulation, and thinning the endometrium
options.B: By increasing estrogen production to flush out the fertilized egg
options.C: By neutralizing male sperm cells directly inside the vaginal canal
options.D: By stimulating sudden contractions that empty the uterine cavity

explanation: Think of the progestin hormone as a triple-security system: it blocks sperm from entering, stops the ovary from releasing an egg, and makes the womb lining cozy-free for implantation! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h2)

question: What constitutes a complete emergency referral system in community midwifery?

options.A: Advance communication, transport arrangements, and patient accompaniment
options.B: Writing a referral note and telling the family to find their own way
options.C: Waiting until the patient loses consciousness before calling for help
options.D: Treating all surgical emergencies at the primary health center

explanation: A successful referral requires more than a note; it involves preparing transport, notifying the receiving hospital, and ensuring clinical continuity. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h6)

question: A patient just returned to the ward after a cerebral angiogram through the groin. What is a key nursing duty?

options.A: Checking the puncture site for bleeding and checking pulses below it
options.B: Restricting all drinking water for 24 hours
options.C: Removing the pressure bandage within the first ten minutes
options.D: Telling the patient to get up and walk around immediately

explanation: Always keep an eye on the puncture site and check the foot pulse to catch any bleeding or clotting early! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T8#GNS222_U3_T8_h4)

question: Why is getting too cold (cold stress) so dangerous for a newborn baby?

options.A: It permanently damages sweat gland function
options.B: It lowers peripheral blood pressure to zero
options.C: It causes immediate closure of the ductus arteriosus
options.D: It triggers hypoglycemia and metabolic acidosis

explanation: When babies get cold, they burn through their energy and oxygen super fast to stay warm, which leads to low blood sugar and acid buildup. Keep our little ones cozy! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h3)
